# Engineering Practices

## Code Review
Every pull request requires at least one approval before merging into the main
branch. Pull requests that touch authentication, billing, or data deletion logic
require two approvals, including one from a senior engineer.

## Branching Strategy
The team uses trunk-based development. Feature branches should be short-lived,
ideally merged within 2-3 days of being opened. Long-running feature branches
are discouraged due to merge conflict risk.

## Testing Requirements
All new features must include unit tests covering the core logic. Code coverage
for new pull requests should not drop the overall project coverage below 80%.
Critical paths (payments, auth, data pipelines) require integration tests in
addition to unit tests.

## Deployment
Deployments to production happen through the CI/CD pipeline only. Manual
deployments to production are not permitted

deployments to production are not permitted except during a declared incident,
and must be logged in the incident channel afterward.

## On-Call
Engineers on the on-call rotation are expected to acknowledge production alerts
within 15 minutes during business hours and within 30 minutes outside business
hours. On-call rotations are weekly and are compensated with a stipend.

## Incident Response
Any production incident affecting customers must be logged with a severity level
(SEV1-SEV3) and a post-incident review must be completed within 5 business days
for SEV1 and SEV2 incidents.

# Remote Work Policy

## Eligibility
Employees who have completed their 3-month probation period are eligible to work
remotely. New hires are expected to work from the office during their first 90 days
to support onboarding and team integration.

## Hybrid Schedule
The default company policy is a hybrid model: employees are expected to be in the
office at least 2 days per week, with Tuesday and Thursday designated as core
in-office collaboration days. The remaining days may be worked remotely.

## Fully Remote Requests
Employees who wish to work fully remotely must submit a request to their manager
and to HR, explaining the business justification. Fully remote arrangements are
reviewed on a case-by-case basis and are subject to role requirements.

## Equipment
The company provides a laptop, monitor, and a one-time home office stipend of
$500 for employees working remotely more than 2 day

, monitor, and a one-time home office stipend of
$500 for employees working remotely more than 2 days per week. Requests for
additional equipment should go through the IT helpdesk.

## Working Hours While Remote
Remote employees are expected to be reachable during core hours, 10 AM to 4 PM
in their local time zone, regardless of their broader working schedule.

## International Remote Work
Working remotely from a country other than the employee's registered work location
requires prior approval

remotely from a country other than the employee's registered work location
requires prior approval from HR and Legal, due to tax and compliance implications.
Such requests must be submitted at least 4 weeks in advance.

## Leave and Time Off
Contractors are not entitled to the company's paid annual leave, sick
leave, or parental leave benefits described in the Leave Policy, as
contractors are not employees. Time off for contractors is governed
entirely by the terms of their individual contract or Statement of
Work. Contractors should coordinate planned absences directly with
their engagement manager.

# Leave Policy

## Annual Leave
Every full-time employee is entitled to 24 days of paid annual leave per calendar year.
Leave accrues monthly at a rate of 2.0 days per month. Unused leave can be carried
forward into the next year, up to a maximum of 5 days. Any leave beyond that cap is
forfeited unless approved by a manager for exceptional circumstances.

## Sick Leave
Employees receive 10 days of paid sick leave per year. Sick leave does not carry
forward and resets on January 1st. For absences

paid sick leave per year. Sick leave does not carry
forward and resets on January 1st. For absences longer than 3 consecutive days, a
doctor's note is required before returning to work.

## Parental Leave
Primary caregivers are entitled to 16 weeks of paid parental leave. Secondary
caregivers are entitled to 4 weeks of paid leave. Parental leave must be taken
within 12 months of the child's birth or adoption date.

## Requesting Leave
All leave requests must be submitted through the HR portal at least 5 business days
in advance, except for sick leave, which can be reported on the day of absence.
Leave requests are approved by the employee's direct manager.

## Public Holidays
The company observes 12 public holidays per year, aligned with the local national
holiday calendar. Employees required to work on a public holiday are compensated
with a substitute day off within 30 days.
